title: Bootstrapping side projects to profit: how Pieter Levels grew Nomad List solo to ~$500K/year
summary: Pieter Levels walks through his 12 startups in 12 months experiment and how Nomad List grew without funding, events or paid marketing. He lays out five stages (idea, build, launch, grow, monetize) and argues for solo building, repeated launches, organic growth and charging from day one.

principles.text: Build for your own problems; you're the best first customer.
principles.quote: you're the expert on your own problems like you can figure out what to make you're the best customer for that product if you make it for yourself

principles.text: Start with a small niche and a story hook, then expand the niche later.
principles.quote: start small first so you can get bigger later because if you want to compete with big companies on the first day it's not going to work

principles.text: Build it yourself and work alone early to keep the feedback loop instant.
principles.quote: you need to have this fast feedback loop where you so if you do yourself like literally I make change like I wake up and I make the button green and that's my work like takes five seconds

principles.text: Validate with a buy button before building the real payment flow.
principles.quote: if you build MVP at a buy button it's so important you know see what people will pay for and the buy button doesn't even have to work

principles.text: Keep relaunching: ship new features and spin-offs every few months and pitch each as a story.
principles.quote: instead of launching one time you launch like every few months you have a new feature you launch it uh send send it to the press send it to all the big reddits

principles.text: Charge from the start and skip paid traffic so you learn if people truly want it.
principles.quote: charge early on and don't be don't be so afraid to charge it's so important
